Guide wall

The space of the excavated soil is immediately filled with slurry (ρ = 1.03–1.12 g/cm³). It presses on the wall of the trench from inside and keeps out the groundwater – until the concrete is in place.
Grab
Cyclic work: lowering – bite – lifting – emptying – lowering again. A bite is typically 2.8–2.9 m long: this is the width of the open grab.
The groundwater presses on the wall of the trench from outside; below the groundwater table the water pressure increases linearly with depth: σ<sub>v</sub> = (z − h)·γ<sub>v</sub>.
Head advantage
The slurry level in the trench must always be at least 1.0–1.5 m above the groundwater table. As the slurry is only slightly heavier than water, this level difference “wins” the pressure contest.
The top 30–50 cm of the wall is mixed with slurry and is broken back; the panels are tied together by a reinforced concrete capping beam, to which the superstructure connects.

A continuous wall of reinforced concrete panels, 40–120 cm thick. Stiff and watertight – here it is also the permanent side wall of the underground car park, and it carries down the load of the building above.
Floor slabs
The floor slabs of the garage levels prop the wall. In top-down construction they are built from the top down: excavation of the pit proceeds below the slabs.
The diaphragm wall is built relatively free of noise and vibration, and it is a stiff wall: so it can be built right next to a building standing on the site boundary.

P1 – first bite

The grab starts at one end of the primary panel: lowering – bite – lifting – emptying. The space of the excavated soil is immediately filled with bentonite slurry, and the slurry level stays near the top of the guide wall throughout.
P1 – second bite
The other end of the panel comes next. A bite is typically 2.8–2.9 m long – the width of the open grab.
P1 – biting out the middle
The roughly 1.4 m wide block of soil remaining between the two end bites is also removed: so this 7.0 m panel consists of three bites.
Concreting P1 with two tremie pipes

Concreting proceeds continuously from the bottom up. The heavier concrete displaces the slurry, which is pumped back to the plant. The ends of the pipes stay immersed in the fresh concrete throughout.
The other primary panels: P2, P3
P2 and P3 are made the same way. Between the primary panels one panel length of soil stays in place – the secondary panels, of similar length, will be here.
Biting out the secondary panels
S1 and S2 are opened the same way, with three bites each: the secondary panels are as long as the primary ones. The stop ends guide the grab and protect the concrete of the finished primary panels.
Reinforcing and concreting the secondary panels
The stop ends are pulled out – the joint is sealed by the swelling waterstop embedded in the concrete – the cages are lifted in, and concreting follows. The wall is now continuous.
The wall is finished: capping beam
The top 30–50 cm of the panels is weak concrete mixed with slurry: it is broken back, and the wall is tied together by a reinforced concrete capping beam. The guide walls can be demolished.
